Brings back the server-backed features that died in **Twitter 9.44 for iOS** once Elon
swapped out the endpoints the old app talks to. Search works again, photo-only posts
render, quote-tweet lists load, and replies actually post.

Built and tested against Twitter 9.44 (`com.atebits.Tweetie2`), which is the last
twitter version iOS 14 supports. You can use this tweak on non ios 14 as well if you
miss the bird :)

## What it fixes

- Word, hashtag and cashtag search
- Top / Latest / Photos / Videos tabs
- Search pagination — scrolling past the first page of results
- Photo-only posts rendering instead of coming up blank
- Quote-tweet lists
- **Replies** — they post, *and* the app accepts the result instead of throwing
  "Tweet not sent" at you

The only thing that doesnt work is DMs cuz the current XChat/encrypted backend is a
completely different problem and out of scope here.

## How it works

### Search — `/search/adaptive.json` is gone

Legacy adaptive search requests get rewritten to the current `SearchTimeline`
GraphQL operation, with the old `tweet_search_mode` / `result_filter` parameters
mapped onto the current `product` values (Top, Latest, Media, People). The response
comes back as a modern GraphQL timeline, so it's converted the other way, into the
`globalObjects` + `addEntries` adaptive shape 9.44 expects, including the cursor
entries that make pagination work.

Two things worth knowing if you want to poke at this yourself: current `ApiPlace`
geometry can carry a bounding-box layout that 9.44's `TwitterPlaceBoundingBox` decoder
force-casts to the old nested-array contract and dies on, so geo fields are stripped;
and users now arrive with `core` / `avatar` / `relationship_counts` objects instead of
the flat `legacy` user, so those get translated back field by field.

### Replies

9.44 posts replies to `api.twitter.com/graphql/…/CreateTweet` with its own persisted
document. That now fails attestation (GraphQL error 37) no matter which document ID
you use, and `/1.1/statuses/update.json` is a flat 404. So the reply is rerouted to
the current X web `CreateTweet` operation during TNL's request-hydration phase, using
the account cookies already sitting in Twitter's own sandbox. Nothing is synthesized,
stored or logged, and if there's no authenticated web session the request is left
exactly as it was rather than half-bridged.

Rerouting alone still wasn't enough, and this was the mad annoying part: the reply
*posted*, then the app threw "Tweet not sent" and offered a retry — which posted a
duplicate. The web response is shaped differently from what 9.44's generated GraphQL
models decode:

- there's no `__typename` on `data.create_tweet.tweet_results.result`, and the legacy
  `TweetResults` union needs it to pick a variant
- the author comes back in the current user shape instead of the legacy `ApiUser`
  fields under `legacy`

So the model builder returned nothing and the app assumed the post had failed.
TwitterRepair converts the result back: restores `__typename`, keeps `rest_id`, rebuilds
the author through the same translation the search adapter uses, forwards only the keys
with a stable legacy contract, and drops unions the old client can't resolve such as
`edit_control`. Genuine server errors are passed straight through, so duplicate content
still gets Twitter's normal "You already said that" alert instead of a fake success.

### Photos — `pic.x.com`

`pic.x.com` display links are exposed to the old entity model as `pic.twitter.com`,
which is all it takes for photo-only posts to render again.

## Keeping it alive

X rotates its persisted GraphQL query IDs. If replies or search break again, pull the
current ones and update the constants at the top of `Tweak.x`:

```sh
python3 tools/extract_web_graphql_ids.py CreateTweet DeleteTweet SearchTimeline
```

Python 3 standard library only, no cookies or account credentials involved — it just
reads the public web bundle. Note the search bridge deliberately keeps its own
`SearchTimeline` document, which still resolves on `api.twitter.com`; the web ID is a
separate value.

## Logs

```
<Twitter data container>/Documents/twitterrepair.log
```

High-level state only: which bridge fired, adapted item counts, server error codes, and
whether the reply conversion ran. No cookies, CSRF values, headers, search terms, tweet
text or response bodies are ever written.

## Build

```sh
# rootless (Dopamine, palera1n rootless, roothide, ...)
make package FINALPACKAGE=1 THEOS_PACKAGE_SCHEME=rootless

# rootful (checkra1n, unc0ver, palera1n rootful, ...)
make package FINALPACKAGE=1 THEOS_PACKAGE_SCHEME= ARCHS=arm64e
```

arm64 + arm64e for rootless, arm64e-only for rootful, deployment target iOS 14.0.
The filter is `com.atebits.Tweetie2` and nothing else — it never injects into
SpringBoard.

### v1.1.0

Restores search, replies, quote-tweet lists, and photo-only posts in
Twitter 9.44 (com.atebits.Tweetie2) after X retired the endpoints the
old app talks to.

Two packages:
- `iphoneos-arm64.deb` — rootless (Dopamine, palera1n rootless, roothide, ...)
- `iphoneos-arm64e.deb` — rootful (checkra1n, unc0ver, palera1n rootful, ...)

See the README for how each bridge works and what's logged.
